question: Does a charging-service merger raise total surplus after joint pricing, procurement efficiencies and the real integration cost?
population: 100,000 potential 10-kWh charging occasions in 100 separate fictional markets

economic_model.driver_choice: Choose one of three 10-kWh charging services or the outside option. Utility is 3 + 0.6*quality - 0.8*price + xi + epsilon. The outside option has deterministic utility zero; all epsilon are independent type-I extreme value with unit scale.
economic_model.firm_choice: Each original firm chooses the price of its service to maximize market_size*(price-marginal_cost)*share. Merged firms jointly choose their two prices and retain both services.
economic_model.information: Drivers and firms observe service quality and current prices; firms observe their own cost and market demand. The analyst observes product-market prices, shares, service quality, ownership, potential market size and the excluded procurement-price shifter.
economic_model.identification: The procurement-price shifter changes marginal cost and equilibrium prices. It is drawn independently of observed quality and unobserved demand. Exogenous quality and an intercept join that excluded shifter in demand IV moments. Markets are independent; demand shocks include a market component shared by all three products.
economic_model.equilibrium: Simultaneous differentiated-product Bertrand pricing. Each service has a constant marginal cost within the operating week. Market size and outside choice remain fixed across scenarios.
economic_model.welfare: Per-occasion consumer surplus is log(1+sum(exp(delta)))/alpha, with alpha equal to the positive magnitude of the fitted price coefficient. Product profits are (price-cost)*share. Multiply each by its market size, then deduct the scenario's real integration cost once from aggregate producer and total surplus.
economic_model.objective: The authority compares baseline total surplus with the fully integrated merger's total surplus. A strictly positive fitted net gain selects approval; an exact tie selects the baseline.
economic_model.mechanism_comparison: The ownership-only scenario measures the joint-pricing response at baseline recovered marginal costs. The full merger adds the adopted procurement savings and integration cost. The same fitted demand and population define all three outcomes.

estimation.interval_family: pointwise normal intervals for the fitted demand coefficients
estimation.counterfactual_estimation: reuse the same native fitted demand for ownership-only and full-merger scenarios

internal.initial_question: How much does the merger raise charging prices?
internal.upstream_comparison: Prices change driver participation, substitution and firm profits. Procurement efficiencies save real resources; integration uses real resources. The net-surplus question determines the adopted approval choice on one population and horizon.
internal.decisive_calculation: Estimate demand with the independent procurement shifter, recover baseline costs, solve joint prices at baseline and reduced costs, and compare consumer plus producer surplus net of the integration cost.
internal.source_status: The economy, seeds, attributes, shock distributions, efficiency and integration cost are independently specified inputs. Data and numerical findings will be generated by the example's producing code.
internal.inference_scope: Coefficient intervals describe independent-market sampling variation under the stipulated logit and IV design. Scenario welfare and the approval comparison are fitted-model point calculations. These intervals are not counterfactual-welfare or selected-decision intervals.
internal.invariants: All scenarios retain the population, quality, demand shocks, outside option and three services. Procurement efficiencies apply to the two merged services only. The rival's recovered marginal cost remains fixed.
internal.validation: Verify key uniqueness, 300 product-market rows, 100 market rows, native coefficient/covariance identities, share inversion, original ownership-adjusted profit gradients, Hessians, and consumer-plus-producer surplus accounting. Retain raw full-precision values and all scientific diagnostics privately.
